question: If I'm held in jail awaiting trial, how long can I be held before I must be indicted and tried, and what happens if that deadline passes?

groups: shall not apply to such period of time
without the consent of the accused

gold_sections.why: The trial clock: five months (in custody) or nine months (on bail) from the probable cause finding on an adult felony, or from indictment if there was no preliminary hearing, or from the arrest if the indictment came first (a detainer is not an arrest); misdemeanor appeals; the excluded delays; and the remedy of being forever discharged from prosecution.

The indictment clock for a jailed accused: release from jail if no presentment, indictment or information is found or filed by the end of the second term of court; exceptions; re-jailing after indictment.
What a 'term' of circuit court is: fixed by each circuit's chief judge, at least four terms a year.
An indicted accused in custody shall be tried within the time limits fixed in 19.2-243.

A motion to dismiss for violation of the constitutional speedy trial right or 19.2-243 must be raised by written motion before trial in circuit court, at least seven days before trial or when its grounds arise, whichever is later.
Continuances for an unavailable lab analyst (excluded from the 19.2-243 clock by its item 5) are capped at 90 days total when the accused is held continuously in custody.
Stops the 19.2-243 clock from the Commonwealth's notice of pretrial appeal until 60 days after the appellate mandate.
In a felony case the Commonwealth may take a pretrial appeal from a dismissal for denial of a speedy trial under 19.2-243, so a dismissal is not final until that appeal is resolved.

Subsection C: a judge may adjourn a pending trial no more than 10 days at a time without the accused's consent, the only statutory limit on delay for a misdemeanor tried in district court (19.2-243 covers adult felonies and misdemeanor appeals).

nuggets.text: A person in jail on a charge that a district court has certified or transferred to circuit court must be discharged from jail if no presentment, indictment or information is found or filed before the end of the second term of the circuit court at which he is held to answer.
nuggets.quote: shall be discharged from imprisonment if a presentment, indictment or information be not found or filed against him before the end of the second term of the court at which he is held to answer

nuggets.text: The indictment deadline does not apply if the court finds Commonwealth material witnesses were enticed or kept away or prevented from attending by sickness or inevitable accident, or in the sanity and competency evaluation cases of 19.2-168.1 and 19.2-169.1.
nuggets.quote: unless it appear to the court that material witnesses for the Commonwealth have been enticed or kept away or are prevented from attendance by sickness or inevitable accident

nuggets.text: Release under the indictment deadline is release from jail, not dismissal: the person can be jailed again once a presentment or indictment is found.
nuggets.quote: A discharge under the provisions of this section shall not, however, prevent a reincarceration after a presentment or indictment has been found.

nuggets.text: The chief judge of each circuit fixes the circuit court's terms, and there must be at least four terms of court each year.
nuggets.quote: The chief judge of each circuit shall fix the terms of each of the courts within his circuit; provided, that there shall be at least four terms of court each year

nuggets.text: For an adult charged with a felony, if the accused is held continuously in custody after the district court finds probable cause, he is forever discharged from prosecution for that offense unless trial begins in circuit court within five months of the probable cause finding.
nuggets.quote: Where a district court has found that there is probable cause to believe that an adult has committed a felony, the accused, if he is held continuously in custody thereafter, shall be forever discharged from prosecution for such offense if no trial is commenced in the circuit court within five months from the date such probable cause was found by the district court

nuggets.text: If the accused is not in custody but is released on recognizance (bail) to appear in circuit court, the limit is nine months from the probable cause finding.
nuggets.quote: if the accused is not held in custody but has been recognized for his appearance in the circuit court to answer for such offense, he shall be forever discharged from prosecution therefor if no trial is commenced in the circuit court within nine months from the date such probable cause was found

nuggets.text: If there was no preliminary hearing, or the accused waived it, the five-month and nine-month periods run from the date the indictment or presentment is found.
nuggets.quote: If there was no preliminary hearing in the district court, or if such preliminary hearing was waived by the accused, the commencement of the running of the five-month and nine-month periods, respectively, set forth in this section shall be from the date an indictment or presentment is found against the accused.

nuggets.text: For a misdemeanor or traffic infraction appealed (or certified) to circuit court, the accused is forever discharged if the new trial does not begin within five months of the conviction or certification when held continuously in custody (nine months if on recognizance).
nuggets.quote: the accused shall be forever discharged from prosecution for such offense if the trial de novo in the circuit court is not commenced (i) within five months from the date of the conviction or certification if the accused has been held continuously in custody

nuggets.text: Time does not count against the deadline when the failure to try the accused was caused by listed reasons: competency or insanity evaluation or restoration or hospital confinement; Commonwealth witnesses kept away or prevented by sickness or accident; a separate trial granted at the request of anyone indicted jointly with others for a felony (including the accused); defense continuances; certain lab-analyst or records-custodian continuances; a hung jury; or a natural disaster, civil disorder or act of God.
nuggets.quote: The provisions of this section shall not apply to such period of time as the failure to try the accused was caused

nuggets.text: Delay caused by a continuance the accused or his lawyer asked for, agreed to, or failed to object to in time (and delay from escaping or failing to appear) does not count.
nuggets.quote: By continuance granted on the motion of the accused or his counsel, or by concurrence of the accused or his counsel in such a motion by the attorney for the Commonwealth, or by the failure of the accused or his counsel to make a timely objection to such a motion by the attorney for the Commonwealth

nuggets.text: Time while any appeal is pending in an appellate court is not counted.
nuggets.quote: But the time during the pendency of any appeal in any appellate court shall not be included as applying to the provisions of this section.

nuggets.text: A trial counts as commenced when jeopardy would attach or when the defendant tenders a guilty or no-contest plea.
nuggets.quote: a trial is deemed commenced at the point when jeopardy would attach or when a plea of guilty or nolo contendere is tendered by the defendant

nuggets.text: Once a felony indictment is found, an accused in custody may be tried at the same term and must be tried within the 19.2-243 time limits.
nuggets.quote: the accused, if in custody, or if he appear according to his recognizance, may be tried at the same term and shall be tried within the time limits fixed in § 19.2-243

nuggets.text: A motion to dismiss because the speedy trial right or 19.2-243 was violated must be raised in writing, before trial, in circuit court.
nuggets.quote: Such a motion or objection in a proceeding in circuit court shall be raised in writing, before trial.

nuggets.text: Continuances because the person who performed a lab analysis is unavailable may total no more than 90 days when the accused has been held continuously in custody (180 days otherwise).
nuggets.quote: Any continuances ordered pursuant to this subsection shall total not more than 90 days if the accused has been held continuously in custody

nuggets.text: If the indictment or presentment was found before the accused was arrested for the offense, the five-month and nine-month periods run from the date of the arrest on it.
nuggets.quote: If an indictment or presentment is found against the accused but he has not been arrested for the offense charged therein, the five-month and nine-month periods, respectively, shall commence to run from the date of his arrest thereon.

nuggets.text: Lodging a detainer (for example against someone already jailed on another charge) is not an arrest, so it does not start the trial clock.
nuggets.quote: The lodging of a detainer or its equivalent shall not constitute an arrest under this section.

nuggets.text: When the Commonwealth takes a pretrial appeal, the time from its notice of appeal until 60 days after the appellate court's mandate does not count toward the 19.2-243 deadline.
nuggets.quote: The provisions of § 19.2-243 shall not apply to the period of time commencing when the Commonwealth's notice of pretrial appeal is filed pursuant to this chapter and ending 60 days after the Court of Appeals or Supreme Court issues its mandate disposing of the pretrial appeal.

nuggets.text: In a felony case the Commonwealth may appeal, before trial, a circuit court order dismissing the charge because the defendant was denied a speedy trial.
nuggets.quote: In a felony case a pretrial appeal from a circuit court may be taken by the Commonwealth from: 1. An order of a circuit court dismissing a warrant, information or indictment, or any count or charge thereof on the ground that (i) the defendant was deprived of a speedy trial

nuggets.text: In circuit court the motion is due at least seven days before trial, but a speedy-trial motion may instead be filed whenever its grounds arise before trial, whichever is later.
nuggets.quote: not later than seven days before trial in circuit court or, if made under clause (ii) of subsection A, at such time prior to trial in circuit court as the grounds for the motion or objection shall arise, whichever occurs last

nuggets.text: A judge may not adjourn a trial pending before him for more than 10 days at a time without the accused's consent.
nuggets.quote: A judge may adjourn a trial, pending before him, not exceeding 10 days at one time, without the consent of the accused.

deadline.anchor: the term of circuit court at which the jailed accused is held to answer (a presentment, indictment or information must be found or filed before that second term ends, or the accused is released from jail)

the district court's probable cause finding on an adult felony (or the indictment, if there was no preliminary hearing or it was waived; or the arrest on the indictment, if the indictment came first), for an accused held continuously in custody; trial must commence
the probable cause finding (or indictment, or arrest on an earlier indictment), for an accused not in custody but recognized to appear in circuit court; trial must commence
the misdemeanor or traffic conviction (or certification) appealed to circuit court, for an accused held continuously in custody; trial de novo must commence
total of continuances for an unavailable lab analyst when the accused is held continuously in custody
after the appellate mandate disposing of a Commonwealth pretrial appeal (the time from the notice of appeal to then is excluded from the 19.2-243 clock)
each adjournment of a pending trial without the accused's consent

amount.value: at least 4 terms of circuit court each year, fixed by the circuit's chief judge

answer:
Virginia has two clocks. Indictment: if you are jailed on a charge sent to circuit court, you must be released if no indictment, presentment or information is filed by the end of the second term of court at which you are held to answer [N1]. Each circuit's chief judge sets at least four terms a year [N4]. Exceptions: missing Commonwealth witnesses and certain competency or sanity evaluations [N2]. Release is not dismissal; you can be re-jailed once indicted [N3].

Trial: for an adult felony, if you stay jailed after the district court finds probable cause, trial must begin within five months (nine if on bail) [N5][N6][N13]. Without a preliminary hearing, the clock starts at indictment [N7], or at arrest on it if indicted first [N16]; a detainer is not an arrest [N17]. If jailed, a misdemeanor appeal gets five months from conviction [N8]. A district court judge cannot postpone a trial more than 10 days at a time without your consent [N21]. Trial begins when jeopardy attaches or you plead guilty or no contest [N12]. Listed delays do not count [N9]: continuances you request, agree to or fail to object to [N10], appeals [N11][N18], and lab-analyst continuances (at most 90 days in custody) [N15].

If the trial deadline passes, you are forever discharged from prosecution for that offense [N5], though the Commonwealth may appeal a felony dismissal [N19]. Raise it by written motion before trial [N14]: at least seven days ahead, or when the grounds arise if later [N20].

out_of_corpus.what: The federal constitutional speedy trial right, which applies separately from the statutory deadlines (including to misdemeanors tried in district court, which have no statutory trial deadline) and is judged by a balancing test (length of delay, reason, assertion of the right, prejudice)
out_of_corpus.where: Sixth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution; Barker v. Wingo, 407 U.S. 514 (1972)

out_of_corpus.what: The actual dates of each circuit court's terms (which determine when the 19.2-242 indictment deadline falls)
out_of_corpus.where: Each chief circuit judge's order fixing the terms of court, abstracted in the Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia (17.1-517) and posted by the circuit court clerk

out_of_corpus.what: Case law, not a court rule (the schema has no case-law kind): how delay is attributed to the defense or the Commonwealth when continuances overlap, what counts as a timely objection, and how the general computation rules (1-223 calendar month; 1-210 A not counting the day of the triggering event) apply to the five- and nine-month periods
out_of_corpus.where: Decisions of the Supreme Court of Virginia and Court of Appeals of Virginia interpreting 19.2-243

local_option: The chief judge of each circuit fixes the dates of the circuit court's terms (at least four a year, 17.1-517), so how many months the 19.2-242 'second term' indictment deadline allows varies by circuit and by when in the term the case was certified.
notes: Two different remedies: 19.2-242 (no indictment by the end of the second term) only releases the accused from jail and allows reincarceration after indictment; 19.2-243 (no trial within five or nine months) forever bars prosecution for that offense, subject to the Commonwealth's pretrial appeal in a felony case (19.2-398 A 1, with the appeal period plus 60 days excluded by 19.2-409). The deadline is counted in terms because a regular grand jury sits at each term of circuit court unless the court finds one unnecessary (19.2-193). 19.2-243 covers adults charged with felonies after a district court probable-cause finding (or indictment without a preliminary hearing) and misdemeanor or traffic appeals and certifications to circuit court; it sets no deadline for misdemeanor trials in general district court, where only the constitutional right and the 10-day adjournment limit of 19.2-183 C apply. An arrest occurs only when the indictment, warrant, information or presentment, or the summons or capias on it, is served or executed (19.2-243, last paragraph). Further exclusions: continuances caused by late notice of insanity, DNA or mental-condition evidence (19.2-168, 19.2-270.5, 19.2-271.6); juvenile transfer appeals (16.1-269.6 F). In circuit court the court may allow a late speedy-trial motion for good cause shown and in the interest of justice; in district court the motion may be raised before or at the proceeding (19.2-266.2 B, D). The state constitutional speedy trial guarantee is Constitution of Virginia, Article I, Section 8 (named in 19.2-266.2 A and 19.2-398 A 1; the out_of_corpus schema has no state-constitution kind). No indictment may be returned before a preliminary hearing on a felony arrest unless it is waived in writing (19.2-218). Juveniles in secure detention must be released if no adjudicatory or transfer hearing is held within 21 days (16.1-277.1), a separate clock. Prisoners held in another state face the Interstate Agreement on Detainers time limits (53.1-210). Sheriffs report semimonthly on prisoners awaiting trial if the chief judge requests (53.1-124 B). The 19.2-187.1 C cap is 90 days in custody and 180 days otherwise; the parallel records-custodian cap is in 18.2-472.1 I. For the same reason the second-term slot stays as the word 'second', and N20's seven-day filing deadline has no slot entry ('7' is inside the '§ 18.2-472.1' and '§ 19.2-187.1' citations in 19.2-243 item 5).
